text:
incident-bot: ALERT: HIGH_ERROR_RATE fired for service=api-gateway route=/v1/generate — 5xx spike (gateway/unavailable) — paging @eng-oncall :rotating_light:

Diego: taking the page, acked. Saw a quick jump to ~7.8% 5xx in last 5m.

Diego: quick log tail for /v1/generate (10m):
```
$ kubectl -n prod logs deploy/gateway --tail=200 --since=10m | grep "/v1/generate"
[2026-03-15T10:10:12Z] POST /v1/generate 502 upstream=upstream-a rt=410ms
[2026-03-15T10:11:03Z] POST /v1/generate 503 upstream=upstream-a rt=180ms
[2026-03-15T10:12:45Z] POST /v1/generate 502 upstream=upstream-b rt=630ms
...
```

Lena: metrics show host flapping in model-hosting upstream-a (connection resets + high latency). Upstream-b has a few hits too.

Joe: I'll verify egress/network path to the model cluster. Diego, is the gateway config recently changed?

Diego: we rolled a small traffic-shaper 40m ago but k8s events show model-hosting endpoints dropping at roughly the same time. Likely provider instability.

Maya: customer impact estimate: ~3% of active users see intermittent failures on generate endpoints, roughly 5% of requests. Not global but customer-facing features could degrade. Filing as Sev3 for now.

Priya: support informed. Will prepare a customer note if we remain degraded beyond 30m.

Diego: mitigation options: 1) rollback traffic-shaper 2) divert a majority of traffic to a fallback model-variant 3) increase gateway retries for transient 502s. Rollback is higher risk.

Lena: recommend traffic split: 75% -> fallback-variant, 25% -> primary for quick relief. Less blast radius than rollback and preserves some capacity on primary.

Diego: applying split via experiments API now. Will add a debug header X-RW-Route to identify backend.

ops-bot: rollout initiated: traffic-split gen-fallback-v1 -> 75% fallback, 25% primary (initiated by Diego). Monitor 5m.

Diego: split live. Observed headers in traces.

[+6m] Diego: 5xx rate reduced to ~1.6% and trending down. Latency for successful requests improved.

Maya: good reduction. Next — alerting: the page was due to alerts at 2% over 5m for /v1/* which tends to upset oncall for transient third-party flaps.

Lena: proposed alert changes: 
- Main generation alert -> evaluate over 10m with threshold 3% (lower severity, avoid paging for short blips).
- Critical customer routes -> 3m window at 5% -> still page oncall (enterprise customers).
- New per-upstream alerts for 5xx so we can label pages as external-provider issues and route to provider alerts rather than oncall immediately.

Joe: also add a small synthetic canary per-region hitting /v1/generate with tight thresholds and three consecutive failures to page. Add dashboard panels showing per-upstream host-count and container restarts.

Priya: will draft customer comms template and add to incident ticket.

Diego: creating follow-up items and quick PRs: 
- infra/alerts/5xx-generate.yaml tweak -> main alert 10m/3%
- infra/alerts/upstream-5xx.yaml -> per-upstream >4% over 5m pages tagged upstream-provider
- infra/dashboards/gen-service.json -> add panel: "Upstream 5xx by host" and "Model-host healthy count"
- infra/synthetics/canaries.yaml -> add global canary for /v1/generate, 30s cadence, alert on 3 fail streak

Lena: add an OpsPager suppression rule to collapse duplicate pages when both gateway and upstream alerts fire (suppress duplicates for 3m).

Diego: PRs in draft: https://git.redwood.internal/r/redwood/infra/pulls/1240 (alerts + dashboard + canary).

Maya: oncall handoff — I'll own the incident for the next 2 hours and start the incident timeline. Diego, please include exact timestamps and the experiment ID in the ticket.

Diego: experiment id: ts-20260315-046, mitigation started 2026-03-15T10:22:30Z. Added debug header samples to the ticket.

ops-bot: Reminder: please add an incident note (brief) within 1 hour to avoid auto-escalation.

Maya: follow-up owners and due dates: 
- Alert tuning + suppression: Lena (EOD)
- Dashboard + synthetic: Joe (tomorrow)
- Customer comms template: Priya (EOD)
- Postmortem: Maya (draft by tomorrow AM)

Lena: quick Q — keep strict paging for hosted enterprise orgs? I recommend yes.

Maya: agreed. Enterprise routes stay strict (3m/5% -> page). General user routes get softer paging. We'll add org labels to alerts.

Diego: current status: mitigation in hold, 5xx steady ~1.4%. Watches for 30m. Will revert split if re-escalation.

Maya: handoff complete, I'm now oncall owner and will update the incident ticket.

Priya: support will send templated notice if not resolved in 30m.

Lena: adding runbook snippet to /docs/runbooks/5xx-upstream.md and linking in ticket.

incident-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigated->watch, severity=3, incident_id=INC-20260315-99.

Maya: leaving thread open for postmortem notes; will close when writeup is done. :white_check_mark:
